body:
I always use an array type in `InjectionToken`'s generic type parameter for multi providers. Then the types align and users of the token can derive it needs to be `multi: true`  

That is not entirely accurate, as a single array value would also be an option, however this is the general problem with providing a value for a token: there's no type safety enforced there.

OK, so specifically I am talking about `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR`. As someone on [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55195456/inject-all-dependencies-registered-under-a-token-through-injector-in-angular/55195518#55195518) pointed out, if the token is typed as `InjectionToken<Foo[]>`, the `get` method behaves correctly.

So the question here is how the Angular team intends the API to work. Depending on that decision the bug is either

1. `Injection#get` is not typed correctly
2. `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` isn't typed correctly
`NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` is not type correctly. Would you mind creating a PR to fix it?

issue.title: fix(forms): type NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR injection token correctly

fixes #29351

- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?

`NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR` is typed `ControlValueAccessor`. This conflicts with it being used as `multi: true` when injecting it programmatically through `Injector#get` as the function is typed to return a single `ControlValueAccessor`, even though it should be an array of them.

Issue Number: #29351


## What is the new behavior?

The injection token is now typed `ControlValueAccessor[]`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No


## Other information

I have not added any tests for this as it's purely a type information. This cannot be tested in an assertion kind of test, the only possibility would be a nop `Injector#get` call and making sure the TS compiler doesn't complain. This isn't a functional test, though, and I doubt we generally test that types are correct, so it seems unnecessary.
